rootNote: Teaching root set by the tutor (GKC Paradigm G) and checked against WLC counts (OSHB 3d15126, verb tokens incl. suffixed forms): H5437 סָבַב, 156 tokens (Qal 89, Hiphil 32, Niphal 20, Poel 12, Hophal 2, Piel 1), the most frequent geminate root with no second weakness and attested in the most stems. It is the paradigm root of GKC Paradigm G, Davidson §42 (Qal/Niphal/Hiphil/Hophal) and K&J. Squares סבב does not attest take examples from other geminate roots.
source: Forms from GKC §67 + Paradigm G (PDF pp. 478-479) and Davidson, Introductory Hebrew Grammar §42 paradigm (pp. 182-183), both in /workspace/hebrew-books/ and read from page images. Squares the books do not print but K&J, Learning Biblical Hebrew pt. 2, Geminate Verb Chart (p. 379) prints are formBasis 'printed'. Wayyiqtol of Niphal/Poel/Poal/Hitpoel/Hophal, Qal participle fs/mp/fp, Qal passive participle fs/mp/fp and the Poel/Poal/Hitpoel fs -ֶת participles are 'rule'. Not copied from any copyrighted chart.
verificationMethod: Each form was matched (consonants + vowel points, accents ignored, dagesh lene and plene/defective ḥolem, shureq and ḥireq-yod spellings normalized) against OSHB morphhb-wlc tokens with the same OSHB morph slot; the Piel/Pual/Hitpael rows match OSHB Poel/Polel (m/o), Poal/Polal (M/O), Hitpoel/Hitpolel (z/r). R1 and every R2 are positional (ס, ב); everything else must agree letter for letter; the Hitpoel row is also matched with ת/R1 in the other order (sibilant metathesis). The example root was checked against its Strong's headword (R1 R2 R2); first radical not guttural/נ/י/ו, R2 not guttural/א/ה/ו/י. Ketiv excluded. Imperatives may carry paragogic ה; infinitives construct may carry a preposition. Example preference: teaching root, then another geminate root; each in order no prefix, ו, preposition. Every matched token was cross-checked against STEPBible TAHOT; tokens where TAHOT disagrees are never used as examples.

notes.aramaizing: Aramaizing forms (GKC §67): in Qal, Hiphil and Niphal-like imperfects the first radical is doubled instead of the second: Qal יִסֹּב beside יָסֹב, wayyiqtol וַיִּסֹּב, Hiphil יַסֵּב beside יָסֵב. GKC and Davidson print them in a second column; they are attested alternates here (only where WLC attests them).
notes.stative: Stative geminates: perfect קַל, תַּם (GKC Paradigm G; Davidson קַל, קַלָּה; K&J 'Stative' column), imperfect יֵקַל. Note only.
notes.contraction: Qal perfect 3rd person of transitive verbs usually uncontracted (סָבַב, סָבְבָה, סָבְבוּ); contracted סַב, סַבָּה, סַבּוּ also occur (GKC §67). Here: uncontracted main, contracted alternate.
notes.pielPilpel: Besides Poel, geminates also have regular Piel (הִלֵּל, קִלֵּל) and Pilpel (גִּלְגֵּל) (GKC §67). Note only; OSHB Piel (p) and Pilpel (l) tokens are never examples for the Poel row.
notes.fsParticiple: Niphal and Hiphil fs participles are printed only as -ָה (נְסַבָּה, מְסִבָּה) and are main. Hophal fs is K&J's מוּסַבָּה. Qal/Poel/Poal/Hitpoel fs follow the -ֶת ruling (rule), with K&J -ָה alternates where K&J prints them.

stemNotes.Piel: Poel (Pôʿēl) in the Piel row: geminates commonly form the intensive as Poel, ō after R1 and R2 written twice (GKC §67). OSHB stem codes m (Poel) and o (Polel) are both matched.
stemNotes.Pual: Poal (Pôʿal) in the Pual row: passive of Poel (GKC §67). OSHB stem codes M / O.
stemNotes.Hitpael: Hitpoel (Hitpôʿēl) in the Hitpael row: reflexive of Poel; with ס the ת metathesizes (הִסְתּוֹבֵב). OSHB stem codes z / r.
